C-FLUSH-AND-PAY.Summary: Two deliverables, chartered by the maintainer as one bundle. First, flush the staged buffer: `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` holds sixteen entries, `F205` through `F220` (measured 2026-09-09 at `65c99ecefe689e5da5e4370bbf79faeee991502f` — the buffer's own header agrees: sixteen, `F205` through `F220`, the authority having corrected its stale count at source before this revision; see Assumptions). They become sixteen `Finding` elements in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml` and sixteen index `Entry` lines in `decisions.xml`, written by hand with the findings base read back from the file and every persisted ceiling held. Second, pay `F205` by minting one chartered registry row for the already-archived `C-INDEX-METRIC-2`, whose `Pays` names exactly `F205` — the row is the only route at HEAD, because the derivation reads registry rows in both layers and no longer reads any archived spec's prose (the prose-mint pass is gone since `C-RECORD-PARSE`, PR #82; `PAID_FINDING_RE` survives only as historical prose inside fixture record copies, searched at this commit). Minting the row makes `F205` eligible immediately, so one `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire` run closes the bundle's own window: it moves exactly two elements — the `F205` finding, stamped `<PaidBy>C-INDEX-METRIC-2</PaidBy>` and landed in `findings-retired.xml`, and the freshly minted row itself, whose name equals an archive directory — flips the `f205` index `Entry` layer in place, and re-derives the live roots. Derived and then driven end to end on a throwaway copy of the record with the shipped CLI at this commit: the flush's findings mid-state base reads back 7715 against the held ceiling 7846 (margin 131 lines); the index mid-state is 272 live `Entry` children against 296 (margin 24); the registry mid-state is 13 live rows against 26. After the move the roots read `findings 7673 / 173 / 7846`, `index 271 / 25 / 296`, `registry 12 / 14 / 26` (byte-identical to today's root), with `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` byte-identical throughout, a second `--retire` reporting moved 0, and the preservation and citation validators green on the moved record. Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30 (scoped, not skirted — the record is this bundle's deliverable), D11, D27. Name searched 2026-09-09 at this commit: no archive directory and no `Row` in either registry layer carries C-FLUSH-AND-PAY; the name is new.
C-FLUSH-AND-PAY.Problem: The staged buffer is the authority's hold-out area under the D30 freeze: entries staged there are not in the record until a flush lands them. Sixteen entries sit staged (`F205` through `F220`, measured by parsing the buffer with the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown`, which parses the buffer as staged — the authority repaired the buffer's two anchor-adjacency defects at source before this revision; see Assumptions). Two pressures make this the moment. One: the findings genre holds real headroom again — `base="7139" headroom="707" ceiling="7846"` at this commit, median element 35 lines under the shipped counting rule, so the payment of `F205` is what frees room no longer; the room already exists and the sixteen entries fit inside it with margin, measured per element below. Two: `F205` is the one staged finding that is *paid but unrecorded*. `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` shipped the index-ratchet remedy (live-`Entry` metric, one-time root rewrite, genre-aware diagnostic) and is archived applied (spec and plan `status="applied"`, measured), but it carries no registry row in either layer — searched, zero rows — and the derivation can no longer read its spec's payment prose, so nothing in the record says who paid `F205`. The flush and the payment belong together for an ordering reason the engine forces: the flush puts `F205` live, the mint makes it eligible at once, and the validator reports `finding-eligible-still-live` and `registry-eligible-still-live` until the move runs — so a committed tree can hold neither the live paid finding nor the live archive-named row. The end state, not any intermediate, is the deliverable.

Goals.Goal: The flush of exactly the anchors f205 through f220 — selected by anchor id, never by position. Sixteen `Finding` elements land in `findings.xml` in the house shape the predecessors calibrated (open tag, `<Title>` carrying the heading line, `<Body>` carrying the buffer body, close tag), and sixteen index `Entry` lines land in `decisions.xml` with `layer="live"`, ids `f205` through `f220` in the delimiter-preserving slug form. Bodies embed verbatim from the buffer — the buffer is staged pre-escaped (`<`, `>`, `"` appear in its text exactly as the record stores them; the seventeen raw `&` characters across its five marked-up bodies are the leading bytes of those staged escapes, and no staged body carries a raw `<` or a bare `&` — measured over all sixteen bodies) — and the buffer is measured flush-clean at this revision: sixteen anchors `f205` through `f220`, each immediately adjacent to its heading, zero `[[f…]]`-form references, and the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` parses the buffer as staged with no normalization (driven at this commit). No render-time normalization is applied: the authority repaired the buffer's defects (the two anchor-adjacency violations, `F213`'s raw `<`, the stale header count) at source before this revision, so the two normalizations the predecessor draft bound to the flush have no input — and a renderer rule with no input is scope no criterion in this bundle can honestly exercise, because the buffer is not this bundle's write scope: nothing here can make such a criterion red except by editing a file this spec forbids touching, which is the defect class that cost C-INDEX-METRIC-2 a supersede. An adjacency defect re-staged later is already discriminated loudly by shipped code: `parseFrozenMarkdown` throws `split: missing anchor for heading at line N` when a heading's preceding line is not an anchor (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:182`-185, re-read at this commit), stopping the flush before a mis-sliced body can enter the record; a raw `<` cannot break well-formedness, and matching the record's pre-escaped house form is the buffer's staging convention, the authority's. The citation ruling this bundle adopts: a citation that does not resolve does not enter the record — every fragment citation in the staged bodies is measured resolvable against the index once the flush lands (`f204` and `f136` already index ids; `f205` through `f220` land in the same flush; driven end to end: the citation validator exits 0 on the moved throwaway record), and any staged reference the gate would not resolve is a stop-and-report, never something to normalize away at render. `F216`'s raw `>` characters in `->` arrows are legal character data and are left as-is. The findings root is hand-written from a read-back, never from a projection: base equals the file's `newlineCount` after the write (derived 7715 = 7139 + 576 element lines by the shipped rule and confirmed by read-back on the throwaway drive), headroom equals ceiling minus that base (131), and the ceiling stays 7846. The index root is hand-written the same way: base 272 live `Entry` children, headroom 24, ceiling 296 untouched. A read-back above the persisted ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling.

The minted row, chartered for an already-archived bundle. One `<Row name="C-INDEX-METRIC-2" status="live" kind="chartered">` lands in live `registry.xml`, appended after the last live row, carrying an empty `Number` (the bundle was never in the ratified order), a `Charter` that records the mint search in the house form (**Searched before minting**, dated at this commit, zero prior rows in either layer carrying the name), a `<Pays>F205.</Pays>` whose token set is exactly `F205`, and a `<StatusText>` recording the delivery — archived applied 2026-09-09 as `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` (PR #84) — and that this row was minted post-archive by C-FLUSH-AND-PAY so the derivation can see a payment the archived bundle's own spec names. The StatusText deliberately carries no *Closed with* clause, so the second mint channel (`closedWithTokens` over `StatusText`, shipped at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` in `derivePayerMap`) mints nothing: the row's derived payment set is exactly `F205` through the `Pays` cell alone, measured by the shipped function on an isolated root whose archive contains only the row's name. Minting a row changes the registry's shipped metric — the live `Row` count — and the production roots-invariant tripwire (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2018`-2054, shipped by C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4) requires every live root's `base` to equal its shipped metric read back and `base + headroom = ceiling`, so the registry root is hand-rewritten in the same commit as the mint: base 13, headroom 13, ceiling 26 held. The move's own persist recomputes the root back to 12 / 14 / 26 after the row retires — byte-identical to today's root line, measured on the throwaway drive — so the registry's ceiling is held throughout and the committed end state leaves `registry.xml` with twelve live rows, exactly as it began.

One move, and the end state it must produce. The order is: flush, mint, then a single `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire` in the same execution wave, then validation exits 0. The move is expected to report moved 2 and to write exactly: `F205` spliced to `status="retired"` and stamped `<PaidBy>C-INDEX-METRIC-2</PaidBy>`, landed in `findings-retired.xml`; the `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` row landed in `registry-retired.xml` with `status="retired"` — the row moves in the same run because a live row whose name equals an archive directory is itself eligible, which is the shipped mechanism this bundle's mint deliberately engages; the `f205` index `Entry` flipped to `layer="retired"` in place, the index having no retired sibling and its `Entry` lines staying (C-INDEX-METRIC-2's shipped position); all four live roots recomputed by the shipped `persistSnapshot` — findings `base="7673" headroom="173" ceiling="7846"` (formula ceiling `7715 + 7 × 34 = 7953` clamped to the held 7846), index `base="271" headroom="25" ceiling="296"`, registry `12 / 14 / 26`, rulings `1697 / 186 / 1883` with `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` byte-identical to their pre-move bytes (measured on the throwaway drive; the rulings persist clamps `min(1883, 1697 + 259) = 1883`). Every value above was driven end to end with the shipped CLI on a throwaway copy of the record at this commit — pre-move validate exits 1 with exactly `finding-eligible-still-live` (f205) and `registry-eligible-still-live` (the row), the move reports moved 2, post-move validate exits 0, a second `--retire` reports moved 0 and writes nothing, and the preservation and citation validators pass on the moved record. Anything else the move reports — a third element moved, a byte outside the expected files — is a stop-and-report, not a number to adopt. The intermediate states between flush and move, and between mint and move, are the D28.1 enforcement saying the move is due: declared, verified working-tree states, never a commit `validate:ci` can see.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record the retirement validator governs, the retirement suite, and this bundle's own artifacts; no graph module is written, no `src/` file is edited, and exactly one `scripts/` file is edited (the suite, for the production assertions the criteria name). Roadmap: RM-GOVERNED-PATH (record integrity). Binding live rulings: D28 (every genre carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet — the flush lands inside every persisted window, margins measured in Assumptions), D28.1 (eligibility is the enforcement and the ceiling the backstop; the mid-state eligibility findings are the enforcement saying the move is due), D30 (scoped, not skirted — the record is the deliverable, so the freeze is scoped to the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files: no other dispatch touches the record while a record-writing task of this bundle is in flight, and no brief promises a frozen base across one; findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next staged number, never into the record under edit; no hard Constraint in this spec transcribes a scalar count of any file it changes — the occupancy, wrap and median figures live in Assumptions and expire, and every criterion below asserts a relation its instrument can observe), D11 (nothing deferred here lacks a dependency or a conflict), D27 (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's). The payment set is exactly the token `F205`; no other token is paid by this bundle, and none can be: the payer map at this commit mints 73 tokens from registry rows in both layers and none of them is `F205` through `F220` (measured with the shipped `derivePayerMap`).

Payment evidence, the load-bearing rule, inherited from C-PAYMENT-RECORD, C-PAYMENT-RECORD-2 and C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3 and re-applied to the single token. Sufficient, all of: (1) a present-tree witness — the index ratchet `F205` describes is removed in the present tree, witnessed by the shipped code itself: the index budget is the live `Entry` count behind the module constant `INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES = 40` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:449`-454, whose comment names C-INDEX-METRIC-2), read by the validator's index ceiling check (`checkCeilingValue` on the live-`Entry` count, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1439`), the retire path's index snapshot (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1260`) and the split path's index base, with the genre-aware breach diagnostic at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1539`-1548; (2) the paying bundle is archived applied — `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-INDEX-METRIC-2/spec.xml` and its `plan.xml` both `status="applied"` at this commit; (3) no `Row` in either registry layer carries the name (searched by parse at this commit, zero hits) and the archived spec does not already mint the payment by prose — at HEAD the derivation reads no archived spec at all, the prose-mint pass having been removed by C-RECORD-PARSE (PR #82), so the row is the only route; (4) the finding is live at mint time — the flush puts it there, which is why flush and payment are one bundle. The witness was re-read at this commit; a finding is never evidence of present state, and neither is this spec.

Order, ceiling, and CI. The committed sequence is: (1) the flush, findings first with the base read back, then the index `Entry` lines and the index root read-back; (2) the row mint in live `registry.xml` with the registry root read back; (3) one `--retire` in the same execution wave, before any commit `validate:ci` can see; (4) validation exits 0. A commit that holds the flushed tokens, the live row or any eligible element without the move is ineligible: the validator reports `finding-eligible-still-live` and `registry-eligible-still-live` until the move runs. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. Do not write the row directly into `registry-retired.xml` — `--retire` is the sanctioned writer of the retired sibling and of the `PaidBy` stamp, and the live-then-moved route is the predecessor's shipped shape. A second `--retire` after the move is a byte-level no-op (moved 0, early return before any write, measured), and the close ceremony's own move is a no-op because this bundle's name carries no row (F196's post-close rule).

Write scope, anchors, and imports — enumerated once (F136.1's rule). Files this spec forces into write scope: the record files `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml`, `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `decisions.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `rulings-retired.xml`; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the production assertions, read-only over the record); and this bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-PAY/`. None of the record files carries a `LINKS:` header (re-checked at this commit; the LINKS tokens inside them are prose in finding bodies and row Charters), the suite file carries none either (searched at this commit), and no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` owns any of them — the record and `scripts/` sit outside the graph's path set, and the lint config ignores `scripts/` (`.ngrace-lint.json` `ignoredDirs`). Do not mint a synthetic module, and do not repeat this list as a second module list anywhere. Do not register the record files in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS. Do not add a lint issue code. Escape markup as character data (`<`, `>`, `&`) in every artifact this bundle writes; never paraphrase brackets away.

Buffer handling. The flush set is exactly the anchor ids f205 through f220, matched as `` forms, never by position. Bodies embed verbatim: no render-time normalization exists — the buffer is measured flush-clean (sixteen adjacent anchors, zero raw `<`, zero `[[f…]]`-form references, every raw `&` a staged escape's leading byte), and any non-identity transform of a body byte is a deviation this spec's criteria refuse. The citation rule binds the same way: a staged cross-reference that would not resolve against the index does not enter the record — a stop-and-report, not something to normalize away at render. Nothing in this bundle writes `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`: the authority repaired the buffer's measured defects (the stale ten-entry header paragraph, the two adjacency violations, the one raw `<`, the `[[f…]]` citation forms) at source before this revision, and pruning the flushed entries remains post-merge hygiene owned by the authority, not a task here.

Evidence hygiene, settled lessons. Every token-specific criterion below is observed by a production assertion the later plan adds to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` — read-only walks over the record in the C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2 house shape (its AC-FLUSH and AC-CHARTER assertions are the precedent) plus the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 Goal-4 pattern, and one read-only production run of the shipped `validateRecordRetirement` asserting zero findings; the suite before those assertions exist is not evidence for these claims, because it contains zero occurrences of the flushed ids (F213's law: grep before citing). Each criterion names the mutation that turns its evidence red, and both directions are shown before the artifact is approved. Every `CloseEvidence` `Command` matches a shipped discriminating shape — read at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:100`-177 (`DEFAULT_CLOSE_EVIDENCE_COMMAND_SHAPES`) and `:191`-203 (`closeEvidenceCommandIsDiscriminating`, token-based over flattened text): the bun-test shape for the suite, the grace.ts-lint shape at `--fail-on warnings` for close-time lint, and the `git diff --exit-code` shape with a named baseline commit for every byte-invariance claim (F210's rule). No criterion compares a fixed `git show` against a floating working-tree read (F215): every diff criterion's window is this bundle's own diff, stated in the criterion, probed in the post-close state, with this bundle's own archive directory excluded from archive pathspecs (F188) and tracked paths only (F174). Any test the later plan adds that measures the real repository carries an explicit generous timeout (F185). Every task `Verification` command the later plan records must exit 0 as written at recording time (F184). Task `Verification` and `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root — the command text contains `--assertions current`, or it invokes lint of this root and omits `--assertions` — checked by hand because the shipped detector misses the grace.ts form (F171). Current-mode lint appears only as post-archive AC-CLOSE-LINT. Payer-map measurements call the shipped `derivePayerMap`, and a fixture archive mirrors the real archive membership the claim needs (F212).

NonGoals.NonGoal: Paying `F206` through `F220` or any other token. Owner: those tokens' own future charters; the record's payment audits. Measured at this commit: none of the sixteen staged tokens appears in the payer map the shipped `derivePayerMap` derives over both registry layers, and this bundle's only mint channel carries exactly `F205` — so the move reports moved 2, and a larger number is a stop, not an expectation. The refusal reasons and checks live in the payment-evidence Constraint.

Changing the record engine, the CLI, or any shipped constant: `derivePayerMap`, `PAYER_KINDS`, `persistSnapshot`, the eligibility scans, `checkStatusFile`, the shape check, the ceiling checks and `INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES` already perform every write this bundle needs — the shipped code needs no new change, and no `src/` file and no `scripts/` file other than the one suite file is edited. Owner: unchanged surfaces — no user-visible CLI token, config key, or ngrace command changes.

Writing or pruning `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`. Owner: post-merge hygiene, the authority's. The buffer's measured defects (the stale header count, the two anchor-adjacency violations, the one raw `<`, the `[[f…]]` citation forms) were repaired at source by the authority before this revision; this bundle repairs nothing in the buffer and applies no render-time normalization — the flush embeds the corrected buffer verbatim.

Minting a live chartered row for C-FLUSH-AND-PAY itself, re-flushing any entry already in the record, or minting rows for any other rowless archived bundle. Owner: the authority's flush; this bundle writes only the sixteen staged entries and the one `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` row.

Raising any persisted ceiling, hand-editing a `PaidBy`, re-deriving any ceiling from the current base, or touching any genre's budget, constant, or diagnostic: the findings and rulings line budgets, the registry's live-row budget and headroom, the index's live-`Entry` budget and its clamp — all shipped positions this bundle holds rather than revisits, C-INDEX-METRIC-2's rejection of the re-derivation remedy included. Owner: no one — the standing record rules.

Editing `README.md`, `examples/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plans/README.md`, `skills/ngrace/`, `plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/`, `docs/plans/archive/`, tracked paths under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` except this bundle's own later arrival there, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `.ngrace-lint.json`, or `CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS`, and any fixture under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/`. Owner: unchanged surfaces / the archive rule. Archived specs are never edited to carry a payer phrase — the row is the route, as the maintainer ruled for the predecessors.
